html:
The greatest king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, who ruled from 605 to 562 BCE. As crown prince he beat the Egyptians at the Battle of Carchemish in 605 BCE, which gave Babylon control of Syria and the Levant.

The small kingdom of Judah, part of the land of Israel and Judah, rebelled against him twice. He took Jerusalem in 597 BCE and sent its king and leading men to Babylon. After a second revolt his army destroyed Jerusalem and its Temple in 587 or 586 BCE and deported many more, starting the Babylonian exile. He also besieged the Phoenician city of Tyre for thirteen years.

With the riches of empire he rebuilt Babylon: huge double walls, palaces, the blue-glazed Ishtar Gate and the great temple tower Etemenanki, likely the model for the Tower of Babel. Later tradition credits him with the Hanging Gardens, though Babylonian records never mention them. The Book of Daniel paints him as a proud king humbled by God. His empire fell to Persia only 23 years after his death, when Cyrus took Babylon.
